_comment: Merged into the project's .claude/settings.json permissions.deny by the kickoff skill. Guardrails that need no runtime.
_env_example_comment: Read(./.env.*) also matches .env.example, and that is kept on purpose. Deny beats allow in Claude Code and the patterns have no negation, so the only way to exempt .env.example would be to name each secret file instead - and then a .env.dev nobody listed is readable. A blank form is worth less than that coverage. The cost is that the model cannot Read .env.example either, which the connect command used to assume it could: it now tests for the connector block with grep through Bash instead. If you change this rule, change commands/connect.md in the same commit.
_pipe_comment: Piping the internet into a shell (curl ... | sh) is denied by its right-hand side. Claude Code splits a command at |, &&, ; and the like, and checks each part on its own, so a rule that spells out the whole pipeline can never match anything. The three rules that used to do that - Bash(curl:* | sh) and friends - blocked nothing from the day they shipped. What reaches the rules is curl ... on one side and a bare sh on the other, so the bare shell is what is denied: nobody runs sh with no arguments on purpose, and sh script.sh still works. validate.mjs check 13b refuses a rule with a separator in it.
_powershell_comment: On Windows the PowerShell tool is on by default, and a Bash rule does not cover it. Every git guardrail therefore has a PowerShell twin, which check 13b enforces. irm ... | iex is PowerShell's curl ... | sh; Invoke-Expression also matches its iex alias, since Claude Code canonicalises aliases before matching.
